trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most stunning marine preserves with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational video about the reef is required before entry, making it a fun learning experience for the whole family.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and recover from travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay. Freshen up, unpack, and take a leisurely stroll along the nearby beach to get your bearings. Pick up snacks and supplies at the nearest grocery store (Times Supermarket or Foodland) to stock up for the week and save on meal costs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koko Marina Center (about 5 minutes away) for a casual first dinner. Explore the waterfront area, watch the sunset over the marina, and decompress after your flight.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the airport before landing or skip — arrival is at 1 PM.
meals.lunch: Pick up a plate lunch from a nearby local spot like Zippy's or L&L Hawaiian Barbecue (~$10–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Koko Marina Center food options — try Nico's at Pier 38 or a local poke bowl shop (~$12–$15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Stop at a grocery store on the way from the airport to stock your room with breakfast items (fruit, yogurt, cereal) to save money throughout the trip. Reserve Hanauma Bay snorkeling tickets online as soon as possible — they sell out fast and must be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — one of Hawaii's most iconic marine preserves. Arrive early (opens at 6:45 AM) to beat crowds. Watch the mandatory 9-minute educational video, then spend 2–3 hours snorkeling among sea turtles, colorful reef fish, and coral. Entry fee is $25/adult, free for children under 12.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive or bus to Sandy Beach Park (just 10 minutes east). Watch expert bodyboarders tackle powerful shore break waves — not ideal for swimming but a spectacular spectacle for families. Relax on the wide sandy beach and enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the hotel. Visit Koko Head Crater viewpoint at sunset for panoramic views of the coastline — free and stunning. Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast with groceries purchased yesterday — fruit, yogurt, and granola bars (~$2–$3 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the grocery store to enjoy at Hanauma Bay or Sandy Beach — sandwiches, chips, and drinks (~$5–$7 per person).
meals.dinner: Pick up plate lunches or bento boxes from Fukuya Delicatessen & Catering or a nearby local deli (~$10–$13 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations — book tickets at the official Hawaii DLNR website. Bring reef-safe sunscreen (required at Hanauma Bay), water shoes, and plenty of water. Snorkel gear can be rented on-site for ~$12. Parking at Hanauma Bay is $3.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic Makapuu Point Lighthouse Trail (free, about 20–30 minutes from the hotel). This 2-mile round-trip paved trail offers breathtaking views of the windward coast, sea cliffs, and offshore islands. During August, keep an eye out for humpback whales in the distance. Family-friendly and stroller-accessible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to Waimanalo Beach — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in Hawaii. Enjoy calm, clear turquoise water perfect for swimming, building sandcastles, and picnicking. The beach is long, uncrowded, and completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back along the coast and stop at a shave ice stand in Kailua for a classic Hawaiian treat. Browse the charming Kailua town area before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — toast, fruit, and juice (~$2–$3 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic to enjoy at Waimanalo Beach — deli sandwiches, fruit, and drinks from the grocery store (~$5–$7 per person).
meals.dinner: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — a beloved local deli/café with affordable sandwiches, salads, and hot plates (~$12–$15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Makapuu Trail. Bring hats and sunscreen — the trail is mostly exposed. Waimanalo Beach has restrooms and lifeguards on duty. Shave ice at Aoki's Shave Ice in Kailua is a must-try (~$4–$6 per serving).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie (about 45 minutes north). This is one of Oahu's top family attractions. Explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Daytime admission includes cultural demonstrations, canoe rides, and interactive activities. Look for discounted tickets online (~$60–$70/adult, ~$45–$55/child with basic package).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — catch the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon, try traditional games, and watch artisan demonstrations. This attraction easily fills a full day.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the evening show 'HA: Breath of Life' if budget allows (included in premium packages or ~$20–$30 add-on). Otherwise, head back south and stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck on the North Shore for a legendary budget-friendly dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast before heading out early (~$2–$3 per person).
meals.lunch: Lunch is included in most Polynesian Cultural Center packages — a buffet with Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes (included in ticket price).
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck on the North Shore — famous garlic shrimp plates (~$14–$16 per plate, feeds one generously).

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets online in advance for the best prices. The basic 'Gateway' package is the most budget-friendly option. The drive back from the North Shore in the evening is scenic but can take 1–1.5 hours. Consider carpooling or checking if a shuttle is available from Waikiki.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the North Shore of Oahu — drive to Haleiwa Town, a charming surf town with colorful shops, local art galleries, and a relaxed vibe. Walk along the harbor and browse the local boutiques. Visit Matsumoto Shave Ice, one of the most famous shave ice spots in all of Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waimea Bay Beach Park — a stunning crescent-shaped beach with calm summer waters (August is ideal for swimming here). Families can enjoy cliff jumping from the famous Waimea Rock (for older kids and adults comfortable with heights). Alternatively, relax on the beach and swim in the crystal-clear bay.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward East Oahu via the H-2 freeway. Stop at a local farmers market if one is available (Oahu has several evening markets). Settle in for a quiet evening at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local café in Haleiwa — try Kono's Northshore for breakfast burritos and smoothies (~$8–$10 per person).
meals.lunch: North Shore plate lunch from a food truck near Haleiwa or Waimea Bay — shrimp, fish tacos, or chicken plates (~$10–$13 per person).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the hotel using groceries, or pick up a poke bowl from a local shop near the hotel (~$10–$14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Bay cliff jumping is for strong swimmers and older children/adults only. The water is calm in summer but always assess conditions. Parking at Waimea Bay can be limited — arrive before 10 AM or after 3 PM. Haleiwa is about 1 hour from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument — a short drive from the hotel. Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit of this ancient volcanic crater for panoramic views of Waikiki and the Honolulu coastline. Arrive by 7–8 AM to beat the heat and crowds. Entry is $5/person or $10/car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Waikiki Beach — just 10–15 minutes from the hotel. Enjoy the famous beach, people-watch, and let the kids play in the gentle surf. Walk along Kalakaua Avenue, browse the International Market Place (free to enter), and enjoy the lively atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Waikiki for the evening. Watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Show (free, Tues/Thurs/Sat/Sun at 6:30 PM — check schedule). Enjoy the Friday fireworks at Hilton Hawaiian Village (free to watch from the beach, every Friday at ~7:45 PM).

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast before the early Diamond Head hike (~$2–$3 per person).
meals.lunch: Waikiki food options — try Rainbow Drive-In, a local institution with affordable plate lunches (~$9–$12 per person).
meals.dinner: Waikiki — grab dinner at Marugame Udon (fresh udon noodles from ~$5–$9 per person) or a food truck along Kalakaua Avenue.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head trail is paved but steep in sections — wear good shoes and bring water. The trail includes stairs and a tunnel. Strollers are not recommended. Friday fireworks at Hilton Hawaiian Village are a beloved local tradition — arrive at the beach by 7:15 PM for a good viewing spot.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the KCC Farmers Market at Kapiolani Community College (Saturday mornings, 7:30 AM – 11 AM, free entry). This is one of Oahu's best farmers markets with local produce, fresh-cooked foods, tropical fruits, and handmade goods. A great budget-friendly way to sample local flavors and pick up snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park — a beautiful, family-friendly beach right next to Honolulu. The calm, reef-protected waters are perfect for young children. Enjoy free swimming, picnicking, and relaxing on the large grassy park areas. Afterward, browse Ala Moana Center (the largest open-air shopping mall in the world) — free to walk through and window shop.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Chinatown in downtown Honolulu — a vibrant, historic neighborhood with art galleries, local restaurants, and evening markets. Walk along Hotel Street and Nuuanu Avenue for local culture and affordable dining options.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the KCC Farmers Market — fresh acai bowls, malasadas, and local fruit (~$5–$8 per person).
meals.lunch: Picnic at Ala Moana Beach Park using market finds or grocery store items (~$5–$7 per person).
meals.dinner: Chinatown dinner — try Little Village Noodle House or Fete Hawaii for affordable, delicious local-style meals (~$12–$16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The KCC Farmers Market is extremely popular — arrive early for the best selection. Ala Moana Beach Park has lifeguards, restrooms, and showers. Chinatown can be lively on weekend evenings — it's safe and family-friendly in the early evening hours.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walking tour of the historic Iolani Palace and the surrounding Capitol District in downtown Honolulu. The exterior and grounds are free to explore. If interested in the interior tour, tickets are ~$22/adult and ~$6/child — a worthwhile educational experience for families. Nearby is the King Kamehameha Statue, perfect for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum (about 20 minutes from the hotel) — Hawaii's premier natural history and cultural museum. Explore Hawaiian artifacts, a real Hawaiian royal feather cloak, planetarium shows, and Science Adventure Center exhibits. Admission is ~$26/adult and ~$19/child — look for online discounts or BOGO deals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the East Oahu area for a relaxed evening. Visit Koko Head District Park or take a sunset drive along Kalanianaole Highway for beautiful coastal views. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast (~$2–$3 per person).
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, affordable lunch near Bishop Museum — try a nearby plate lunch spot or bring a packed lunch (~$7–$10 per person).
meals.dinner: Local favorite near the hotel — try Ono Hawaiian Foods in Kaimuki for authentic Hawaiian cuisine like kalua pig and poi (~$12–$15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Iolani Palace exterior and grounds are always free. The Bishop Museum is best enjoyed with at least 3–4 hours. Check the Bishop Museum website for any free admission days or family discount promotions. Ono Hawaiian Foods is cash-only and very popular — arrive early or expect a short wait.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hanauma Bay for a second snorkeling session if you loved it the first time — or try snorkeling at Shark's Cove on the North Shore (free, great for families with older kids). Alternatively, spend the morning at Lanikai Beach in Kailua — a postcard-perfect beach with powdery white sand and calm, clear water, completely free to access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayak to the Mokulua Islands (the 'Mokes') from Lanikai Beach. Rent kayaks from Kailua Beach Adventures (~$30–$40/hour for a double kayak). Paddle to the small offshore islands, explore the beach, and snorkel in the surrounding waters. A memorable family adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kailua town for the last time — browse local shops, grab shave ice, and enjoy a relaxed dinner. This is a great evening for souvenir shopping at affordable local boutiques.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast or grab malasadas from a nearby bakery (~$1–$2 each) — Leonard's Bakery is a must-try Hawaiian institution.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the beach and kayak adventure — sandwiches and snacks from the grocery store (~$5–$7 per person).
meals.dinner: Kailua — try Cinnamon's Restaurant for a relaxed family dinner, or grab affordable plate lunches from a local food truck (~$10–$14 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has limited parking — arrive early or park along nearby residential streets and walk. Kayak rentals require advance booking during peak season (August). The paddle to the Mokulua Islands is about 20–30 minutes each way — suitable for families with children 8 and older who are comfortable on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — take one last sunrise walk along the beach near the hotel. Collect shells, take photos, and soak in the views of the ocean. Visit any last-minute spots you missed, or simply relax and enjoy the scenery. Pack up and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. If time allows before heading to the airport, make a quick stop at a local ABC Store or Longs Drugs for affordable Hawaiian souvenirs (macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, chocolates) — much cheaper than airport shops.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Honolulu International Airport (Daniel K. Inouye International Airport). Carry memories of beautiful beaches, vibrant marine life, and rich Hawaiian culture.

meals.breakfast: Final in-room breakfast using remaining groceries, or treat the family to a sit-down breakfast at Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen in Kailua — famous for macadamia nut pancakes (~$10–$14 per person).
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable airport lunch or grab takeout from a nearby spot before heading to the airport (~$10–$13 per person).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM — confirm with your hotel. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Honolulu airport, especially during peak summer travel season. Use any remaining cash or gift cards at local shops before departing. Mahalo for an amazing trip!

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands; clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay (approx. 30–45 min from HNL airport).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk along the coastal area near Hanauma Bay. Enjoy the scenic overlook of Hanauma Bay crater from the ridge viewpoint — a stunning first impression of East Oahu without the full commitment of a snorkeling session today.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Koko Marina Center or Hawaii Kai Town Center for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the waterfront promenade, pick up any essentials from a local grocery store, and settle in for an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy snacks or a meal on the plane before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a casual spot like Panda Express or Zippy's near the airport on the way to the hotel.
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company at Koko Marina Center — family-friendly atmosphere, fresh local craft beers for adults, and a solid menu of burgers, pizza, and fish tacos. Mid-range pricing (~$15–$25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Reserve your Hanauma Bay snorkeling reservation online tonight for Day 2 — entry is limited and sells out quickly. Reservations open 2 days in advance at 7:00 AM HST. Pick up sunscreen (reef-safe only is required at Hanauma Bay) and water shoes if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — arrive early (gates open at 6:45 AM) to beat the crowds. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then spend 2–3 hours exploring the stunning reef ecosystem. The bay's calm, shallow waters make it ideal for all ages and skill levels. Spot sea turtles, parrotfish, and hundreds of tropical species.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive the scenic Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail (approx. 10 min from the bay). This easy 2-mile round-trip coastal hike offers panoramic views of the windward coast, sea arches, and in August, possible humpback whale sightings offshore. Suitable for families with children.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rinse off and relax. Drive to Kailua Town (approx. 20 min) for a charming small-town evening stroll and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Prep a light breakfast at the boutique stay or stop at Longs Drugs / 7-Eleven nearby for yogurt, fruit, and granola bars — eat before Hanauma Bay opens.
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch to enjoy on the beach at Hanauma Bay (no food allowed on the beach itself, but picnic tables are available in the park area). Alternatively, stop at Zippy's on Kalanianaole Highway on the way back.
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua — a beloved local institution with steaks, fresh fish, and salads. Casual but flavorful. (~$20–$35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires reef-safe sunscreen only — no oxybenzone or octinoxate. Snorkel gear can be rented on-site (~$12/set). The bay is closed on Tuesdays, so today is perfect timing. Bring cash for parking ($3) and gear rental.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Waikiki Beach (approx. 25–30 min from East Oahu) for Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach. Book a group lesson with a certified instructor — Waikiki's gentle, rolling waves and sandy bottom make it the world's best beginner surf spot. Lessons typically run 1.5–2 hours and include board rental. Kids as young as 5 can participate.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, stroll along Kalakaua Avenue, Waikiki's famous beachfront boulevard. Visit the Duke Kahanamoku Statue, browse local shops, and let kids splash in the calm waters near the Waikiki Beach Center. Visit the nearby Waikiki Aquarium (small but excellent for families — $12 adults, $5 kids) in the early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Waikiki sunset from the beach, then head to the Royal Hawaiian Center or Kalakaua Avenue for dinner and shopping. Watch the free hula and live music performances at the Royal Hawaiian Center's Royal Grove (most evenings around 6:00–7:00 PM).

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua (on the way) — famous for their red velvet pancakes and local-style breakfasts. A family favorite. (~$12–$18 per person).
meals.lunch: Grab plate lunches from a beachside food truck or window near Waikiki Beach — look for garlic shrimp, kalua pork bowls, or spam musubi. Budget-friendly (~$10–$15).
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — wildly popular, cafeteria-style Japanese udon restaurant. Enormous portions, fresh noodles, and extremely affordable (~$8–$12 per person). Expect a short line but it moves fast.

day_by_day.notes: Book surfing lessons in advance — Hans Hedemann Surf School and Waikiki Beach Services are both reputable and family-friendly (~$40–$60/person for group lessons). Apply sunscreen generously before lessons. Parking in Waikiki can be expensive — use the Waikiki Trade Center garage or consider taking TheBus from East Oahu.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore (approx. 50–60 min from East Oahu via H-3 and H-2). Start with a visit to Waimea Valley — a beautiful botanical garden and cultural heritage site with a 45-foot waterfall you can swim under. Family-friendly, shaded trails, and rich Hawaiian history. (~$20 adults, $10 kids).
day_by_day.afternoon: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour at North Shore — head to Haleiwa Town and dive into the legendary North Shore food truck scene. Sample shave ice at Matsumoto's or Aoki's (a rite of passage), fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from Giovanni's Shrimp Truck, and acai bowls. Stroll through Haleiwa's charming surf shops and art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline) on the way back to admire the coastline — in August, the water is calm and swimmable on the North Shore. Watch the golden-hour sunset before driving back to East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the boutique stay or grab malasadas (Portuguese doughnuts) from Leonard's Bakery on the way through Honolulu (~$1.25 each — a must-try Hawaii treat).
meals.lunch: North Shore food trucks in Haleiwa — Giovanni's Shrimp Truck for garlic shrimp plates (~$14), followed by Matsumoto's shave ice (~$4–$6). This IS the food tour.
meals.dinner: Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa — famous for slow-roasted kalua pork burritos and breakfast plates. Casual, delicious, and very affordable (~$10–$15). Eat before heading back, or pick up something light near the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: North Shore surf conditions in August are typically calm (big wave season is November–February), making it safe for family swimming at Sunset Beach. Haleiwa can get busy on weekends — a Wednesday visit is ideal. Bring cash for food trucks. The drive back via Kamehameha Highway along the east coast offers spectacular ocean views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Windward Coast — drive to Kailua Beach Park (20 min from the hotel), consistently rated one of the best beaches in the US. The powdery white sand and turquoise water are ideal for swimming, building sandcastles, and kayaking. Rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards locally and paddle out to the Mokulua Islands (the 'Mokes') — a stunning twin-island sea bird sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Byodo-In Temple in the Valley of the Temples (approx. 15 min from Kailua). This stunning replica of a 900-year-old Japanese Buddhist temple nestled against the Ko'olau Mountains is peaceful, photogenic, and fascinating for all ages. Feed the koi and peacocks on the grounds. (~$5 adults, $2 kids).
day_by_day.evening: Relax evening at or near the boutique stay. Walk along the coast near Hanauma Bay at dusk for a quiet local experience.

meals.breakfast: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — beloved neighborhood deli and café with fresh pastries, sandwiches, and coffee. Perfect pre-beach fuel. (~$8–$14).
meals.lunch: Picnic on Kailua Beach — pick up fresh poke, sandwiches, and drinks from Whole Foods Market or Kalapawai Market before heading to the beach.
meals.dinner: Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen in Kailua — famous for macadamia nut pancakes and hearty local comfort food. Open for breakfast and lunch only, so alternatively try Cactus Mexican Grille in Kailua for flavorful, family-friendly Mexican food with a Hawaiian twist. (~$15–$22 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals to the Mokes are available through Kailua Beach Adventures (~$69/double kayak for half day). The paddle is about 1.5 miles each way — suitable for families with older kids (8+). Life jackets provided. Book in advance. Byodo-In Temple opens at 9:00 AM and is best visited in the morning for softer light and fewer visitors.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu (approx. 25 min from East Oahu) — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. World-class exhibits on Hawaiian royalty, Polynesian navigation, volcanic geology, and Pacific island cultures. Excellent for families with interactive science exhibits and a planetarium. (~$25 adults, $17 kids).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park — a long, calm, reef-protected beach adjacent to Ala Moana Center. Perfect for swimming, picnicking, and relaxing. Afterward, browse Ala Moana Center, the largest open-air shopping mall in the US, for souvenirs, local brands, and treats from the food court.
day_by_day.evening: Catamaran Sunset Sail with Whale Watching — board a family-friendly catamaran from Honolulu Harbor or Waikiki for a breathtaking 2-hour sunset cruise. In August, look for spinner dolphins and green sea turtles; humpback whale season peaks in winter but occasional sightings occur year-round. Enjoy complimentary snacks and drinks aboard as the sun sets over Diamond Head.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the boutique stay or stop at Liliha Bakery (near the Bishop Museum) — a Honolulu institution famous for their coco puffs and pancakes. (~$10–$16).
meals.lunch: Ala Moana Center food court — excellent variety including Panda Express, Makai Market food court with local plate lunch vendors, or grab fresh poke from Foodland Farms inside the mall. (~$10–$16).
meals.dinner: Enjoy pupus (appetizers) and light snacks on the catamaran, then have dinner at a waterfront restaurant near Kewalo Basin — try Lure Fish House for fresh Hawaiian seafood in a relaxed, upscale-casual setting. (~$25–$40 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran sunset sail in advance — popular operators include Maita'i Catamaran and Na Hoku II (~$45–$65 adults, $30–$40 kids). Sails typically depart around 5:00–5:30 PM and last 90 minutes to 2 hours. Bring a light layer as it can be breezy on the water. The Bishop Museum is best visited on a weekday to avoid school group crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Polynesian Cultural Center on the North Shore (approx. 45 min from East Oahu). Spend the morning exploring the six authentic Pacific island villages — Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, Aotearoa (New Zealand), and Hawai'i. Watch live cultural demonstrations including fire-making, canoe paddling, and traditional weaving. This is one of Hawaii's top family attractions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — catch the afternoon canoe pageant on the river, watch the IMAX film on Polynesian voyaging, and enjoy the interactive village activities. The center is expansive and easily fills a full day.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — the evening culminates in the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' luau show. Enjoy an all-you-can-eat Hawaiian buffet featuring kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and more, followed by a breathtaking 90-minute theatrical performance with fire dancers, drummers, and over 100 performers. One of Hawaii's most memorable family experiences.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the boutique stay before the drive — fruit, granola bars, or a quick stop at a nearby café.
meals.lunch: Dining included with the Polynesian Cultural Center package — the Gateway Buffet on-site offers a variety of Hawaiian and Pacific island dishes. (~included in admission or ~$15–$20 add-on).
meals.dinner: Luau buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — fully included with the evening package. Feast on traditional Hawaiian foods in an authentic outdoor setting.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the full Ambassador Package for the best experience (~$120–$160 adults, $80–$110 kids) — it includes all-day village access, the IMAX film, the evening luau, and the 'Ha: Breath of Life' show. Book well in advance as Saturday evenings sell out. The center is operated by Brigham Young University–Hawaii and is alcohol-free. Plan to arrive by 12:00–1:00 PM for the full experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — enjoy a slow start at the boutique stay. Take a gentle morning swim or snorkel at a nearby beach like Alan Davis Beach or Kawaiko'i Beach near the hotel. These quieter spots offer a more local, uncrowded experience compared to Hanauma Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (approx. 20 min from East Oahu). Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit of the volcanic crater for sweeping 360-degree views of Waikiki, Honolulu, and the Pacific Ocean. The trail involves stairs and a tunnel but is manageable for most families. (~$5/person entrance fee).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Kapiolani Park area at the base of Diamond Head. The park hosts local families, food vendors, and occasional live music on Sunday evenings. Stroll through the Honolulu Zoo grounds exterior or relax on the grass before heading back to East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the boutique stay — pick up fresh tropical fruits (papaya, pineapple, mango) from a local farmers market or grocery store the day before.
meals.lunch: Diamond Head Market & Grill near the trailhead — a beloved local deli with excellent plate lunches, fresh poke, and sandwiches. Very popular with locals. (~$12–$18).
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai — a legendary Hawaii Regional Cuisine restaurant by chef Roy Yamaguchi, located near the hotel. Upscale-casual with fresh fish, creative Hawaiian fusion dishes, and beautiful Ko'olau Mountain views. A mid-range splurge night. (~$35–$55 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head trail reservations are required and must be booked online in advance at hawaiistateparks.org. The trail opens at 6:00 AM — an early start beats the heat and crowds. Bring water and wear closed-toe shoes. Roy's Hawaii Kai is a special treat and worth the slightly higher spend — make reservations in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hanauma Bay for a second snorkeling session — now that you're more familiar with the bay, venture slightly deeper toward the Witches Brew or Keyhole areas (with a guide or experienced swimmer) for more diverse marine life. Alternatively, explore the tide pools at the eastern end of the bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Sea Life Park Hawaii (approx. 10 min from the hotel on the Windward Coast) — a marine attraction featuring dolphin encounters, penguin feeding, sea turtle exhibits, and a Hawaiian monk seal sanctuary. Interactive and educational for all ages. (~$40 adults, $25 kids). Book a dolphin interaction experience for an unforgettable family memory.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drive along the Makapu'u coastline — stop at Sandy Beach Park to watch local bodyboarders riding the powerful shore break (do not swim here — it's for experienced bodyboarders only, but spectacular to watch). End the evening with a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before Hanauma Bay — try Keneke's BBQ in Hawaii Kai for a local plate lunch spot that also serves breakfast, or pick up malasadas from a nearby bakery.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for Hanauma Bay — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks from the local grocery store. Eat at the park's picnic area after snorkeling.
meals.dinner: Ono Hawaiian Foods in Honolulu (if willing to drive 20 min) — an authentic, no-frills Hawaiian food institution beloved by locals. Try laulau, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia. Very affordable (~$12–$18). Or stay local at Koko Head Café in Kaimuki for creative brunch-style dinner plates.

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park's dolphin interaction programs must be booked in advance and fill up quickly (~$150–$200/person for the swim-with-dolphins experience, or ~$80 for a shallower interaction). Standard park admission alone is worthwhile even without the add-on programs. Sandy Beach Park has some of the most powerful shore break in Hawaii — supervise children carefully near the water.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take one last swim or stroll along the East Oahu coastline near the boutique stay. Visit the Hanauma Bay ridge overlook one more time for a farewell view of the stunning crater bay. Pack souvenirs and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique stay and drive toward Honolulu for final souvenir shopping. Stop at Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (if open — Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday) or head to the International Marketplace in Waikiki for last-minute gifts: Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, Hawaiian quilts, aloha shirts, and local art. Pick up fresh-baked goods from Liliha Bakery or Leonard's Bakery as edible souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (HNL) with plenty of time before your departure flight. Enjoy a final shave ice from a cart near the airport or a last plate lunch from one of the airport's local food options inside the terminal.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the boutique stay or a nearby café — try Crepes No Ka Oi in Kaimuki for sweet and savory crepes with local ingredients. A memorable last morning meal. (~$12–$18).
meals.lunch: Highway Inn in Kaka'ako — one of Honolulu's most authentic Hawaiian food restaurants, serving traditional dishes like pipikaula, laulau, and haupia since 1947. A perfect final Hawaiian meal. (~$15–$22).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner before heading to HNL. Makai Market food court at Ala Moana Center (near the airport route) offers excellent last-minute local options if time permits.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight for check-in, security, and customs at HNL. The airport has improved dining options post-security including local favorites like Lāhaina Chicken Company and Honolulu Cookie Company for final treats. Don't forget to declare any agricultural items — fresh fruits and plants cannot be taken off the island without inspection. Mahalo for a wonderful trip to Hawaii!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most stunning marine preserves with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational video about the reef is required before entry, making it a fun learning experience for the whole family.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian and Polynesian culture with a beachfront luau featuring traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, and an all-you-can-eat Hawaiian feast including kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. Kids will love the interactive cultural village activities during the day.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take beginner-friendly surfing lessons right on the iconic Waikiki Beach, one of the most gentle and ideal surf spots in the world for first-timers. Certified instructors cater to all ages including young children, and most participants are standing on their boards within the first lesson. Boards and rash guards are included.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour at North Shore
experiences.description: Stroll along the famous North Shore food truck scene and indulge in Hawaii's iconic shave ice, fresh garlic shrimp plates, acai bowls, and malasadas. This self-guided foodie walk along Kamehameha Highway lets families sample the best of local Hawaiian cuisine in a relaxed beachside atmosphere with stunning ocean views.

experiences.name: Catamaran Sunset Sail with Whale Watching
experiences.description: Board a family-friendly catamaran for a breathtaking sunset cruise along the coastline, with opportunities to spot humpback whales (seasonal, November–April), spinner dolphins, and sea turtles. Snacks and non-alcoholic beverages are included for kids, and the crew shares fascinating facts about Hawaii's marine life and history throughout the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Honolulu International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique hotel and settle in. Enjoy a leisurely welcome orientation with complimentary tropical refreshments and a private tour of the property. Take a gentle stroll along the shoreline near Hanauma Bay to acclimate to the island atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the hotel's private dining terrace or a short drive to Alan Wong's Honolulu — one of Oahu's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants featuring locally sourced Hawaiian Regional Cuisine. Toast to the beginning of your Hawaiian adventure.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the flight or light snack upon arrival — hotel welcome fruit platter and refreshments provided
meals.lunch: Light bites at the hotel lounge or a quick stop at Kaimana Beach Café en route from the airport
meals.dinner: Alan Wong's Honolulu — signature tasting menu with Hawaiian Regional Cuisine; reservations recommended in advance

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule relaxed to allow for jet lag recovery. Confirm all upcoming experience bookings with the hotel concierge upon check-in. Request early check-in if possible. Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — just minutes from the hotel, this is the perfect first full-day activity. Arrive early (8:00 AM) to beat the crowds and secure the best experience in this stunning marine preserve. A certified guide will accompany the family through the coral reefs teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant marine life. Premium snorkel gear provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a poolside lunch and relaxation. Enjoy the hotel's luxury amenities — spa, pool, or a private cabana session on the beach. Optional: book a 60-minute Hawaiian Lomi Lomi massage at the hotel spa for adults while kids enjoy supervised beach activities.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace followed by dinner at Vintage Cave Honolulu — an ultra-premium, Michelin-recognized restaurant offering an extraordinary multi-course tasting experience in a dramatic underground setting.

meals.breakfast: In-room or hotel restaurant — full Hawaiian breakfast with fresh papaya, macadamia nut pancakes, Kona coffee, and fresh-squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Poolside dining at the hotel — grilled mahi-mahi tacos, tropical salads, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Vintage Cave Honolulu — multi-course chef's tasting menu with wine pairing; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and charges an entry fee. The bay is closed on Tuesdays, so this Monday slot is perfectly timed. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — required by Hawaiian law. Bring water shoes for the family.

day_by_day.morning: Since Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays, head to Waikiki Beach for Surfing Lessons. A private, family-oriented surf school will provide personalized beginner-friendly instruction on the gentle waves of Waikiki — one of the safest and most iconic surf spots in the world. All ages and skill levels welcome. Premium boards and rash guards provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, explore the Waikiki waterfront. Visit the prestigious Royal Hawaiian Center for luxury shopping — browse Tiffany & Co., Chanel, and local Hawaiian designer boutiques. Stop at the historic Royal Hawaiian Hotel (the 'Pink Palace') for afternoon tea or a signature Mai Tai on the oceanfront terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue and dine at Nobu Honolulu at the Nobu Hotel — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion cuisine with fresh Hawaiian seafood in a sophisticated, stylish setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel restaurant — acai bowls, fresh tropical fruit, eggs Benedict with kalua pork, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Royal Hawaiian Hotel's Mai Tai Bar — signature cocktails, fresh poke bowls, and island-style flatbreads with oceanfront views
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — black cod with miso, wagyu beef, and fresh Hawaiian fish carpaccio; cocktail pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Book surf lessons in advance with a premium surf school offering private family sessions (recommended: Hans Hedemann Surf School). Waikiki is approximately 20–25 minutes from Hanauma Bay by private car. Arrange a luxury chauffeur for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hiking experience at Diamond Head State Monument — an iconic volcanic crater with panoramic views of Oahu's coastline. A private guide will lead the family on this historic trail, sharing geological and cultural insights. The hike is moderate and family-friendly (approximately 1.8 miles round trip). Arrive at 7:00 AM to enjoy cooler temperatures and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Kahala neighborhood for a visit to The Kahala Hotel & Resort — even as a non-guest, the hotel's dolphin lagoon is a beloved family experience. Book a premium Dolphin Quest encounter for an up-close, educational interaction with Atlantic bottlenose dolphins. Follow with relaxation on Kahala Beach, one of Oahu's quietest and most exclusive stretches of sand.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at The Kahala Hotel's signature restaurant, The Plumeria Beach House — an elegant oceanfront dining experience featuring contemporary Hawaiian cuisine with fresh local ingredients and stunning sunset views.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before the hike — granola, fresh fruit, and Kona coffee to go
meals.lunch: Post-hike refreshment at Diamond Head Market & Grill — famous plate lunches and fresh-squeezed juices; a beloved local institution
meals.dinner: The Plumeria Beach House at The Kahala Hotel — fresh Hawaiian seafood, prime cuts, and tropical desserts with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head requires advance online reservations. Start early to avoid heat. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. Dolphin Quest at Kahala must be booked well in advance — highly popular with families. Private luxury car recommended for the day's transitions.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the North Shore — depart by 8:00 AM via private luxury van. Visit the famous Shave Ice and Local Food Tour at North Shore: explore the legendary food truck scene at Haleiwa Town, indulge in Hawaii's iconic shave ice at Matsumoto's or Aoki's, sample fresh poke, garlic shrimp from Giovanni's Shrimp Truck, and browse the charming boutiques and surf shops of Haleiwa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the North Shore to Sunset Beach and Banzai Pipeline — even in summer (calmer season), the scenery is breathtaking. Enjoy a leisurely swim or snorkel at Shark's Cove (one of Oahu's best snorkeling spots on the North Shore). Alternatively, book a private guided sea cave kayaking tour along the rugged coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to East Oahu by private transfer. Dinner at Senia — a critically acclaimed, intimate restaurant in Honolulu offering a creative tasting menu with local Hawaiian ingredients prepared with global culinary techniques.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — eggs, toast, tropical fruits, and coffee before departure
meals.lunch: North Shore food experience — Giovanni's garlic shrimp, fresh poke bowls, tropical smoothies, and legendary shave ice for dessert
meals.dinner: Senia, Honolulu — chef's tasting menu; one of Honolulu's most exciting fine-dining destinations; advance reservation required

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is approximately 1 hour from Hanauma Bay. A private luxury van or SUV is ideal for the family. North Shore waves are calm in summer, making it safe for swimming. Bring cash for food trucks — many do not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran charter from Kewalo Basin or Waikiki — a premium, family-exclusive sailing experience along Oahu's stunning coastline. Enjoy snorkeling stops at pristine reefs, look for spinner dolphins and sea turtles, and take in the dramatic views of Diamond Head from the water. Gourmet breakfast and refreshments served on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore by early afternoon. Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum, perfect for families. Explore the Hawaiian Hall, the Science Adventure Center, and the Planetarium. A private guided tour can be arranged for a more immersive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — immerse the family in authentic Hawaiian and Polynesian culture. This world-famous evening features traditional dances from Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, and more, followed by a spectacular iMax-style show and a lavish ali'i luau feast. One of Hawaii's most memorable family experiences.

meals.breakfast: Served on the catamaran — fresh fruit, pastries, yogurt parfaits, and tropical juices while sailing
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Bishop Museum café or a nearby Honolulu restaurant — poke bowls, sandwiches, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional Hawaiian feast with kalua pig, poi, haupia, lomi salmon, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter at least 2 weeks in advance. The Polynesian Cultural Center is located in Laie on the North Shore (approximately 1 hour from the hotel) — arrange private round-trip transportation. The luau evening runs approximately 5:00 PM to 9:30 PM. Book the Ambassador Package for the best seating and VIP access.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury spa morning at the hotel or at the Four Seasons Resort O'ahu at Ko Olina — book a family wellness experience including a couples' massage, kids' spa treatments, and a private oceanfront yoga session. This is a perfect rest and recharge day after six active days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ko Olina Lagoons — four stunning man-made lagoons on Oahu's west coast with calm, protected waters ideal for families. Enjoy paddleboarding, kayaking, and swimming in the crystal-clear lagoons. Rent premium watercraft through the Four Seasons or a private outfitter.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman at Ko Olina — a beloved farm-to-table restaurant with outstanding cocktails, fresh Hawaiian seafood, and wood-fired pizzas in a relaxed yet sophisticated setting. Watch the sun dip below the Pacific horizon.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — full spread with Hawaiian sweet bread French toast, fresh fruit platters, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the Four Seasons Ko Olina — fresh seafood, tropical salads, and refreshing cocktails or mocktails
meals.dinner: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman, Ko Olina — farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine with award-winning mai tais and stunning sunset views

day_by_day.notes: Ko Olina is approximately 45 minutes from Hanauma Bay — arrange private luxury transportation. The Four Seasons Ko Olina spa is world-class and family-friendly. Book spa treatments at least a week in advance. This day is intentionally relaxed as a mid-trip reset.

day_by_day.morning: Private submarine or semi-submarine tour with Atlantis Adventures — depart from Pier 6 in Honolulu Harbor aboard a real submarine that dives 100 feet below the surface to explore coral reefs, tropical fish, sea turtles, and even sunken shipwrecks. A truly extraordinary and unique family experience unlike anything else in Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chinatown Honolulu — a vibrant, historic neighborhood with art galleries, boutique shops, and a thriving food scene. Visit the Honolulu Museum of Art for a curated family tour of its impressive Pacific and Asian art collections. Browse the weekend farmers' market at Blaisdell Center if timing aligns.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style celebratory dinner at Sushi Sho Honolulu — one of Hawaii's most exclusive and sought-after omakase experiences, offering only 10 seats per seating with master sushi chef Keiji Nakazawa. An extraordinary, once-in-a-lifetime culinary event. Reservations must be secured months in advance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light and energizing before the submarine adventure; fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Chinatown Honolulu exploration — dim sum at Legend Seafood Restaurant or fresh ramen at Izakaya Torae Torae
meals.dinner: Sushi Sho Honolulu — world-class omakase tasting experience; 20+ courses of the finest sushi; advance reservation essential (book months ahead)

day_by_day.notes: Atlantis Submarine tours depart multiple times daily — book the earliest available slot. Children must be at least 36 inches tall to participate. Sushi Sho is extremely difficult to book — contact the hotel concierge immediately upon trip planning to secure a reservation. This is widely considered one of the best sushi experiences in the United States.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of Oahu — take to the skies for a breathtaking 60-minute private helicopter tour covering Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountain Range, the North Shore, Pearl Harbor, and the stunning windward coastline. This bird's-eye perspective of the island is an unforgettable family highlight. Blue Hawaiian Helicopters offers premium private charters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a profoundly moving and historically significant site. Tour the USS Arizona Memorial, USS Missouri Battleship, and the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum. A private guided tour provides deeper historical context and a more personal experience. This is a meaningful and educational experience for the entire family.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed final evening. Enjoy a private beachfront bonfire dinner arranged by the hotel — a bespoke, intimate dining experience with a personal chef preparing a Hawaiian feast under the stars on the beach. S'mores, tropical cocktails, and live ukulele music complete the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread; fuel up before the helicopter adventure
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor area — lunch at the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center café or a nearby local restaurant; keep it simple and respectful to the site's atmosphere
meals.dinner: Private beachfront bonfire dinner arranged by hotel concierge — custom Hawaiian menu with fresh seafood, grilled meats, tropical sides, and dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour at least 1–2 weeks in advance and confirm weight limits for all passengers. Pearl Harbor requires timed entry passes — book online in advance. The private beachfront dinner must be arranged with the hotel concierge at least 3–4 days ahead. This is a spectacular penultimate evening experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning snorkel or swim at Hanauma Bay (open again on Tuesdays — wait, note: Hanauma Bay is closed Tuesdays). Enjoy a leisurely final morning at the hotel — sunrise beach walk, last dip in the pool, and a long, indulgent breakfast. Take time to collect any remaining souvenirs from the hotel gift shop or nearby boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final visit to a nearby beach — Sandy Beach Park or Makapu'u Beach for stunning scenery and a last taste of Oahu's natural beauty. Private luxury transfer to Honolulu International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Honolulu International Airport. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Enjoy the airport's dining options or lounge access if available.

meals.breakfast: Grand final hotel breakfast — order everything you loved during the trip; fresh fruit, Hawaiian specialties, Kona coffee, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Casual farewell meal near the hotel or at the airport — fresh poke bowl or plate lunch as a final taste of Hawaii
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner before departure at a nearby restaurant — Roy's Hawaii Kai is a beloved farewell option if time permits (approximately 10 minutes from Hanauma Bay)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay is closed Tuesdays, so plan the final morning as a relaxed hotel experience. Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon beach time. Roy's Hawaii Kai by celebrity chef Roy Yamaguchi is a fitting farewell — book a reservation if the departure schedule allows. Request a late checkout from the hotel if the flight departs in the evening.
